hook.text: Twenty-six words written in 1996 created the modern internet. They also made platforms nearly immune to lawsuits.

buildup.text: Section 230 says platforms aren't liable for what users post. Without it, every company would be sued constantly.

discovery.text: The law was meant to encourage moderation. Platforms could remove harmful content without becoming liable for all of it.

twist.text: Critics say 230 gives platforms a free pass. They profit from harmful content without legal responsibility.

climax.text: Both left and right want to reform 230—for opposite reasons. The left wants more moderation; the right wants less.

punchline.text: One law protects platforms from their own content.

quiz.question: What does Section 230 protect platforms from?
